A king of the Sindhu district and brother-in-law of Duryodhana, having married Duhśalā, daughter of Dhṛtarāṣṭra. [Once while out on hunting, he chanced to see Draupadī in the forest, and asked of her food for himself and his retinue. Draupadī, by virtue of her magical sthālī, was able to supply him with materials sufficient for their break-fast. Jayadratha was so much struck with this act, as well as her personal charms, that he asked her to elope with him. She, of course, indignantly refused, but he succeeded in carrying her off, as her husbands were out on hunting. When they returned they pursued and captured the ravisher and released Draupadī; and he himself was allowed to go after having been subjected to many humiliations. He took a leading part in compassing the death of Abhimanyu, and met his doom at the hands of Arjuna in the great war.]
f. The name of a magical lore (often mentioned with विजया) taught by Viśvāmitra to Rāma, बिद्यामथैनं विजयां जयां च [[
A wife. (The word is thus derived--पतिर्भार्यां संप्रविश्य गर्भो भूत्वेह जायते । जायायास्तद्धिः जायात्वं यदस्यां जायते पुनः ॥ [[

.]]) As last member of Bah. comp. जाया is changed to जानि; सीताजानिः ‘one who has Sītā for his wife’; so युवजानिः, वामार्धजानिः 
-Comp.

-आजीवः 
__1 an actor, a dancer.

-घ्नः 
__1 a murderer of his wife. 
__2 a mole or mark on the body indicative of the death of one's wife. 
-पती (dual) husband and wife. (The other forms of the comp. are दम्पती and जम्पती q. v.)
a. [जि-यत्] Conquerable, vulnerable, that can be conquered (opp. जेय).
